item.text: I’ll add only distinct omissions from the prior coverage, using remembered knowledge and no file reads or source checks.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/103_3/luna/followup.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.5.27	weighed and found lacking	The commentary connects loss, a rightful share, and final reckoning; Daniel says Belshazzar was weighed in balances and found deficient, combining judgment with the market image.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.7.21	doing the Father's will	The commentary identifies the saved by belief together with deeds; Jesus distinguishes saying “Lord” from doing the Father's will.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.1.22	doers of the word	The commentary pairs belief with righteous action; James warns hearers to become doers of the word rather than deceive themselves by hearing alone.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.2	patience bearing with one another	The commentary makes sabr a shared practice; Paul names patience and bearing with one another in love as the conduct that preserves unity.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.18.15	correction that regains a brother	The commentary makes mutual advice a way of holding a community together; Jesus instructs a person to confront a sinning brother privately, and says listening can regain the brother.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.1	restore gently	The commentary joins correction with patience and self-restraint; Paul says to restore a person caught in transgression gently while watching oneself against temptation.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.4.2	correction with patience and teaching	The commentary puts truth before sabr because speaking truth may carry a cost; Timothy is told to reprove, rebuke, and exhort with complete patience and teaching.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.6	love rejoices with truth	The commentary makes haqq the content of mutual counsel; Paul says love does not rejoice in wrongdoing but rejoices with truth.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.7	bearing and enduring	The commentary describes sabr as holding fast for another; Paul says love bears, hopes, and endures all things.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.2.2	works, labor, and endurance	The commentary's traits include work and patience; Revelation praises a church for its works, labor, and patient endurance while testing false claims.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.1.5	faith joined to virtue	The commentary pairs belief with righteous action; Peter urges believers to supplement faith with virtue and knowledge.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.1.6	self-control and endurance	The commentary describes sabr as holding oneself steady; Peter's sequence joins self-control to steadfastness and steadfastness to godliness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.1.7	brotherly affection and love	The commentary's virtues culminate in reciprocal counsel; Peter ends his sequence with brotherly affection and love.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.1.3	trial produces steadfastness	The commentary calls patience a bitter medicine that forms the person; James says the testing of faith produces steadfastness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.1.4	endurance brought to completion	The commentary treats sabr as remaining firm until its work is done; James says steadfastness should have its full effect, making the person complete.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.33.4	estranged brothers embrace	The commentary says patient good can turn enmity into intimacy; Esau runs to embrace Jacob after their long estrangement and fear.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:2Chr.20.20	trust, prophetic counsel, and success	The commentary hears belief as security and counsel as something passed on; Jehoshaphat tells Judah to trust God and the prophets, with the promise that they will stand and prosper.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.3.7	a time to speak and be silent	The commentary joins truthful counsel to self-restraint; Qohelet's paired times for silence and speech give a concrete limit and occasion for words.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.9.10	work while life remains	The commentary ties work to limited time and the day of reckoning; Qohelet urges wholehearted work now, saying there is no work or knowledge in Sheol.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.15.1	a soft answer turns away anger	The commentary imagines truthful counsel replacing dispute; Proverbs says a gentle answer turns away wrath, showing how speech can interrupt conflict.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.25.21	feed a hungry enemy	The commentary says good conduct can turn an enemy into a friend; Proverbs instructs the reader to feed an enemy who is hungry.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.25.22	coals on an enemy's head	The commentary reads kindness toward an enemy as reconciliation; Proverbs adds that feeding the enemy heaps coals on his head, a consequence often read as shame or repentance but whose force is debated.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.2.7	provision through the wilderness	The commentary links trust to safety on a journey; Moses recalls that God accompanied Israel through forty years of wilderness travel and they lacked nothing.
medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 3:2	two people studying together	The commentary makes counsel reciprocal; Avot says that when two sit with words of Torah between them, the divine presence is among them.
medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 4:2	one good deed leads to another	The commentary pictures good action as work that keeps its value and continues; Avot says one commandment brings another and the reward of a commandment is another commandment.
medium	tevrat	motif	Shabbat 127a	kindness and making peace	The commentary replaces a wage formula with mutual responsibility; the Talmud lists acts of kindness and making peace between people among deeds whose fruit is enjoyed now while their principal remains for the world to come.
medium	tevrat	motif	Sirach 2:6	trust and hope in trial	The commentary joins faith to patience under hardship; Sirach tells the one serving God to trust in the Lord, hope in him, and expect his help.
medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 3:9	trust, truth, and abiding	The commentary joins belief with haqq and sabr; Wisdom says those who trust God will understand truth and the faithful will abide with him in love.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.1	run with endurance	The commentary treats patience as staying on a road through hardship; Hebrews urges believers to run the race set before them with endurance.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.3.15	answer with gentleness and respect	The commentary makes truthful counsel a communal duty carried with sabr; Peter says to answer anyone asking about hope with gentleness and respect, keeping a good conscience.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Col.3.13	bear with and forgive one another	The commentary's patience means holding together when people strain one another; Paul tells the community to bear with and forgive one another.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.10.22	endurance to the end	The commentary defines the exception by a completed pattern of belief, action, and patience; Jesus says the one who endures to the end will be saved.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Thess.1.4	faith and endurance in persecution	The commentary says truth may bring hardship that requires sabr; Paul praises the community's steadfastness and faith amid persecutions and afflictions.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Dan.5.27	Aramaic חסר; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary's khusr concerns loss and deficiency; Daniel's Aramaic says the king was weighed and found lacking, a close contextual echo whose root correspondence the table leaves unverified.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Deut.2.7	חסר; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary uses khusr for loss; Deuteronomy says Israel lacked nothing on its wilderness journey, a specific opposite use of the root candidate listed by the table.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:2Chr.20.20	אמנ; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary hears iman as trust and security; this verse repeats the Hebrew root in “trust the Lord” and “be established,” a wordplay relevant to the ayah but not proof of cognacy.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:2Chr.20.20	צלח; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary labels righteous deeds with ṣ-l-ḥ; Jehoshaphat's line ends with the Hebrew verb for prospering, a possible sound correspondence whose biblical sense is success.
EOF"
